questions.question: Antibiotic pharmacokinetics.

parts.text: Give 3 general criteria to step down from IV to PO.

parts_raw.text: 3 General criteria to stepdown from IV to PO

questions.model_answer: a) (1) Fluoroquinolones (2) Metronidazole (3) Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (4) Clindamycin (5) Linezolid. b) (1) Clinically improving/haemodynamically stable and afebrile (e.g., ~24-48 h) (2) Able to tolerate and absorb oral intake (functioning GI tract, no malabsorption or ileus) (3) An available oral agent with adequate bioavailability and spectrum for the pathogen/site of infection.
questions.beyond_mandell: IV-to-PO step-down criteria are not enumerated in this chapter; based on standard antimicrobial stewardship/IDSA switch-therapy principles.

cohort_answer.text: High bioavailability: Clindamycin, Fluoroquinolones, Metronidazole, Rifampin, Linezolid, doxycycline. Stepdown criteria: afebrile (48hr), clinical improvement, able to tolerate GI route, no GI absorption concerns.

questions.question: What are 3 conditions that should be met prior to stepping someone down from IV to PO?

parts.text: What are 3 conditions that should be met prior to stepping someone down from IV to PO?

parts_raw.text: What are 3 conditions that should be met prior to stepping someone down from IV to PO?

questions.model_answer: (1) Clinical improvement with haemodynamic stability (e.g., afebrile ~24-48 h) (2) Able to tolerate and reliably absorb oral medication (functioning GI tract, no malabsorption/ileus) (3) Availability of a suitable oral agent with adequate bioavailability and spectrum for the infection.
questions.beyond_mandell: This chapter does not list IV-to-PO switch criteria; answer based on standard antimicrobial stewardship/IDSA switch-therapy principles.

questions.model_answer: (1) Vancomycin (dosed post-HD) (2) Cefazolin (post-HD dosing, an option for MSSA in dialysis patients) (3) Daptomycin (post-HD dosing). (Ceftriaxone and ceftazidime are further options.)

questions.question: A homeless man presents to the OPAT clinic with purulent cellulitis.
questions.question_raw: Homeless man comes to OPAT clinic. He has purulent cellulitis.

parts.text: What are the two organisms most likely to be responsible?
He remembers that he cut his leg on a seashell by the seashore. You want to cover for Vibrio vulnificus. What is the best oral regimen to empirically cover these organisms?
Give two further regimens that can be IV or oral. If IV they can only be given once per day; if oral they can only be given twice per day. Each regimen can contain a maximum of two drugs.
Name 5 more organisms that can cause marine-associated skin/soft tissue infection.

parts_raw.text: What are the two organisms most likely to be responsible?
He remembers that he cut his leg on a seashell by the seashore. You want to cover for Vibrio vulnificus. What is the best oral regimen to empirically cover these organisms?
Give two further regimens can be IV or oral. If IV can only be given once per day. If po can only be given twice per day. Can only have two drugs max in each regimen.
Name 5 more organisms that can cause “marine associated” skin/soft tissue infection.

questions.model_answer: a) Purulent cellulitis is predominantly staphylococcal: (1) Staphylococcus aureus (the commonest, including MRSA) and (2) group A streptococcus (Streptococcus pyogenes); in direct-sampling series S. aureus (~50%) and GAS (~25%) account for >75% of isolates. b) Doxycycline 100 mg PO BID as single best oral agent – it covers CA-MRSA/MSSA, streptococci, and is first-line for V. vulnificus (tetracyclines are the recognized first-line anti-Vibrio drug). c) (1) Ceftriaxone IV once daily PLUS doxycycline PO BID (ceftriaxone/3rd-gen cephalosporin covers streptococci and Vibrio, doxycycline covers MRSA and Vibrio); (2) Levofloxacin PO/IV once daily PLUS trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole PO BID (levofloxacin covers Vibrio and streptococci, TMP-SMX covers MRSA) – ciprofloxacin is the listed Vibrio alternative. d) (1) Vibrio parahaemolyticus (2) Vibrio alginolyticus (3) Erysipelothrix rhusiopathiae (4) Mycobacterium marinum (5) Aeromonas hydrophila (Streptococcus iniae and Edwardsiella tarda are also acceptable).
questions.beyond_mandell: The IV-once-daily / PO-twice-daily combination regimens in part c are constructed to the question's constraints; Mandell grounds doxycycline + 3rd-generation cephalosporin (or ciprofloxacin) for Vibrio but does not specify these exact dual regimens.
